rationale: The `imports` label had NO oracle in the instrument: `deriveTypeScriptEdges` emits calls/instantiates/uses/references, so every dependency edge this lane emitted — vue alone emitted 2,789 — was stored and compared against nothing, and an invented module or a dropped dependency would have read green. Building `oracles/typescript-imports-exports.ts` found the defect this fixture pins. On a 152-file element-plus draw the oracle agreed with the analyzer on 1,201 of 1,201 NAMED import rows and derived 12 the analyzer did not emit at all: side-effect-only imports. `import './style.css'` has no clause and so contributed no items, and the loop emitted nothing — element-plus's every component does `import '@element-plus/theme-chalk/src/<name>.scss'`, so the style half of every component was invisible. The analyzer now publishes `<specifier>:*` when the `import_clause` is ABSENT, which is what distinguishes a side-effect import from `import {} from "m"` (an empty binding list, not a dependency on side effects). This fixture also pins the rest of the target contract: an alias is not part of the name, because the name is what the EXPORTING module calls it and that is what two files can join on.
